content.content:
#### Chain Steps

An open Chain task lists its steps in its Steps section, beneath its prompt and above its details, in the order they run, each a row as in the list, with its status: its spec step, its code step, and its spec follow-up when it has one. Every step it will run is listed from the moment the chain is sent, while its spec step is still building or running, before any later step has been sent: a step not yet sent is listed all the same, its status a muted "Next" for the one that follows the step running and a muted "Waiting" for any after it, its prompt the chain's, and its time blank until it starts. Each step's row changes in place as the step is sent, queued, runs, and ends, and the list never grows or reorders as a step is sent, only once a step is added, or a spec follow-up is asked for, when it is added at its end. The same holds for the chain's expanded rows in the Running group, and for any task of more than one step. An "Add step" button beneath them adds a step of its own after the last: a Code or a Spec step, chosen from a small menu, with a prompt of its own, typed in the step's row as it expands, its model and effort those of the chain until changed. An added step runs once the step before it finishes, in its own mode's lane and place, as every step of a chain does, told its own prompt, the chain's prompt as typed, and what the step before it replied, as the spec-to-code prompt tells a code step, so a chain can be carried on, as a further code change once the spec is built, or a spec tidy-up after the code. A step not yet sent can be edited, moved among the others not yet sent, or removed; one sent reads as it was. Steps are saved with the chain, in its hidden anchor, as the [PromptSendingScope](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) keeps a queued prompt, so a chain keeps its added steps across restarts, and a step whose step before it failed or was cancelled is never sent, as none of a chain's are.
While it is Running, it is expanded in the Running group: its row, then a row for each of its steps beneath it, in the order they run, sent or still to send, each a 28 pixel row in the same columns, its text set in 16 pixels further and labelled "Spec", "Code", or "Spec follow-up" in that step's mode colour, with the step's own

A chain now lists every step it will run from the moment you send it, not just its spec step. That applies both to its expanded rows in the Running group and to the opened chain's Steps section.

- **Steps not yet sent:** the code step, the spec follow-up when the chain asks for one, and any added steps are listed straight away, while the spec step is still building. They show the chain's prompt and a muted status: "Next" for the step after the one running, "Waiting" for any after that. Their time stays blank until they start.
- **In-place updates:** each step's row changes as it's queued, runs and ends, rather than steps appearing one at a time.
- **Added steps:** in the opened chain they stay editable, and now also show the muted Next or Waiting while the chain runs.
- **Finished chains:** a chain that's over shows only the steps it actually sent.

I differed from the spec on one detail. It says a spec follow-up is added at the end once it's asked for. Whether a chain wants one is known when you send it, so I list it from the start as "Waiting".

The change is in `src/prompt_mode/tasks_tab.rs`. A new test checks that a just-sent chain lists its code step and follow-up in both places. All other tests pass except one about long task output, which also failed in the last two runs and has passed when run on its own.
